parsed.stack: iOS + Android (React Native with a native on-device vision bridge). On-device vision for reading pump switch / pressure tank labels in bad light with no signal, $0 marginal. Occasional cloud call (Haiku-class + one grounded search) only for part-number resolution when back on signal. Everything stored locally, exportable. One-time purchase $19.99 (price_month is that amortised over 12 months).
milestones: Week 1-2: low-light, no-signal capture and on-device label reading for well/septic equipment - torch, glare, condensation are the normal case here.
Week 3-4: the dated record: what is installed, when it was photographed, what changed - built to still make sense 18 months later when something drips.
Week 5: part-number resolution with an honest confidence state, deferred until signal returns.
Week 6: shareable one-page record for the plumber/well contractor (the growth loop).
Week 7: paid unlock after the first free identification, ship to US rural-homeowner subreddits and a well-water forum.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That on-device vision reads a decades-old, corroded pump switch label in a dark crawlspace well enough to name the model, and that the resulting part numbers are actually compatible rather than plausible-looking.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Photograph 30 real well/septic setups (a plumber will let you tag along for a day) in the conditions they actually live in, run the on-device model over them offline, and check the part numbers against a supply-house catalogue.
